assumptions: Reference-honest, macOS-gated. There is no macOS and no iOS simulator in the warp home environment (this repository is Linux), so a live simulator cannot be driven here and the honest evidence is the fake-driver control-logic unit tests, not an operational simulator run. required_evidence is therefore [unit], not operational: claiming a live-simulator run on a Linux box would be a lie the reviewer would correctly reject. The live SimctlDriver (xcrun simctl for boot/launch/terminate/screenshot/video/home-screen backgrounding/appearance, plus an accessibility-bridge seam for tap/type/UI-state assertions that fails loudly when the bridge is absent) is shipped and documented; only its control logic (journey sequencing, lifecycle re-drive orchestration with a provable launch-token restart, device-matrix completeness, and first-failure-named) is gate-tested against a FakeIosDriver with no simulator. Shipped under plugin/templates/scripts/runners/mobile/; not wired into the warp repo's own gate (capabilities: reference). An adopting repo on macOS runs the same runner against a real booted simulator and wires the accessibility bridge.
